0.name: School Quality Reports Data
0.note: The window above must match PROXY_YEAR in schools_validation.py. WARNING: this source holds 404 distinct metrics for school year 2024 and 677 across 2015-2024, and NONE of them measure a building. Checked 2026-08-31 against the words facility, building, clean, safe, maintain, condition, physical, and survey: 0 hits. The metric names cover attendance, test proficiency, course pass rates, and Regents scores. Thus from notebook version 1.2.0 the attendance row is a CONTEXT row and the building record carries the case. The export names the metric in the proxy_metric column, and the proxy name follows the selection. Before notebook version 1.1.0 the export wrote the fixed name school_report_card, which hid which metric the paper cited. Long format. 1 row for each school, metric, and year. The source holds more than 1,000,000 rows, so filter on the server with fetch_metric.

1.name: School Point Locations (APS 2024-08-28)
1.note: Gives each DBN a point. The ATS column is the DBN. Use it to put the proxy on the map. It covers public schools only, so it never matches a private or postgraduate school in the FacDB unit set.

2.name: NYC Building Footprints (BUILDING)
2.note: On disk, pulled 2026-04-12 by data/geo/download_nyc_buildings.py. 1,082,872 footprints and 99.1% carry a usable year; the source writes 0 for an unknown year and _proxies drops it. FacDB gives each unit a BIN, thus this is a key join and not a spatial one. WARNING: a year is NOT oriented. Every other proxy points 'higher is better', so a positive value means agreement. A positive value here says the model calls a NEWER unit better, which is a finding and not a test.

3.name: DOB Violations
3.note: A fault that the Department of Buildings recorded against this building. FacDB gives 99.0% of the schools a BIN, thus this is a key join and not a spatial one. The source holds more than 2,000,000 rows, so the query sends the BIN list of this case to the server and groups there. A category that ends in ACTIVE is an open violation. WARNING: a count rises when a building gets worse, thus _proxies_buildings applies a sign of -1 and the exported value points 'higher is better'.

4.name: DOB ECB Violations
4.note: An Environmental Control Board violation carries a fine, thus it marks a fault that reached a hearing. The status is ACTIVE or RESOLVE. The export adds these counts to the DOB counts, and proxy_source names the 2 ids together.

5.name: DOB Permit Issuance
5.note: A permit says that somebody spent money on this building, thus it is a positive measure and it needs no sign. The count is over the distinct job number and not over the permit rows, because 1 job takes an initial permit, a renewal, and 1 permit for each trade. Job types A1, A2, and A3 only: a new building and a demolition are not investments in the building the model looked at. WARNING: issuance_date holds 2 shapes, MM/DD/YYYY and an ISO timestamp, thus the server cannot filter the year and the module filters it in pandas.

6.name: 2017 - 2018 NYC School Survey Teacher Data
6.note: The only item-level measurement of a school BUILDING that a city school source holds. The value is the share of teachers who agree or strongly agree, from the sheet 'Teacher Pos & Neg %'. WARNING: the asset is an .xlsx blob and not a table, thus SODA cannot query it; _proxies_buildings downloads it to data/external/nyc_school_survey_2018/ and reads the workbook XML. WARNING: the city stopped publishing the item-level survey after 2017-18. The 2019 files (k2zg-756q, uzmq-2khh, 4fcz-jias) hold only the 6 framework scores and no building item. Thus this proxy sits about 7 years before the model run.

7.name: 2017-18 - 2021-22 Demographic Snapshot
7.note: The Economic Need Index of the students who attend the school. It beats tract income as the socio-economic control of this case: a school draws its students from a zone and not from its own block, and a charter or a specialized school draws from the whole city. The source writes a percent string such as 87.9%. WARNING: the index rises with need, thus _proxies_buildings negates it and a positive correlation means the model prefers a school of a wealthier community. This is a CONTROL and not a building measure. 2021-22 is the newest year the source holds.

8.name: DOB NOW: Safety - Facades Compliance Filings (FISP)
8.note: NOT used as a proxy. Local Law 11 applies to a building of more than 6 storeys, and a school is mostly low. Measured 2026-08-31: 189 of the 2,375 school BINs (8.0%) carry any filing. A correlation over 8% of the case would describe the tall schools alone. _proxies_buildings.facade_status_by_bin builds the frame for a reader who wants it, and no export row comes from it.

9.name: 2019 NYC School Survey (student, teacher, and parent files)
9.note: NOT used. Checked 2026-08-31. The 3 files (k2zg-756q, uzmq-2khh, 4fcz-jias) each hold 11 columns: the DBN, the school name, 3 response rates, and the 6 Framework for Great Schools scores. No building item, no cleanliness item. The 3 files also return identical rows, which is a publication fault of the source. The 2017-18 item file (sjxh-har6) is the newest one that names item 6f.
